name: async-whilst-sync-test-serverless-gcf
behavioral_change: In async v_new (3.0.0), the `test` function of `whilst`, `doWhilst`, `until` and `doUntil` changed from a synchronous function returning a boolean to an error-first callback style (`test(cb)` calling `cb(null, condition)`). Function names and argument counts are unchanged and no exception is raised; an old synchronous test ignores the callback it is given, so the loop never enters the iteratee or the final callback and stalls silently.
downstream_effect: serverless-google-cloudfunctions' `monitorDeployment` in shared/monitorDeployment.js polls deployment status with `async.whilst` and resolves a promise from the final callback; after the upgrade the promise never resolves and four jest tests time out. The failure locations all point at the test file shared/monitorDeployment.test.js and jest internals, not at the `async.whilst` call on line 18 that must be edited.
reference_fix: The reference fix changes one line in shared/monitorDeployment.js, replacing the test `() => validStatuses.indexOf(deploymentStatus) === -1` with `(nextTest) => nextTest(null, validStatuses.indexOf(deploymentStatus) === -1)`.
documented_in: The async 3.0.0 CHANGELOG (Breaking Changes) announces that `whilst`, `doWhilst`, `until` and `doUntil` now take asynchronous `test` functions, and the API reference at https://caolan.github.io/async/v3/docs.html#whilst shows the new form `function test(cb) { cb(null, count < 5); }` next to the v2 form `function() { return count < 5; }`. The changelog entry itself contains no code; the code form comes from the API reference of the same version.
failing_tests: shared/monitorDeployment.test.js :: MonitorDeployment > #monitorDeployment() > when monitoring creations or updates > should keep monitoring until "DONE" status is reached
shared/monitorDeployment.test.js :: MonitorDeployment > #monitorDeployment() > when monitoring creations or updates > should throw an error if deployment errors out
shared/monitorDeployment.test.js :: MonitorDeployment > #monitorDeployment() > when monitoring removals > should stop if there are no deployments and the action is "remove"
shared/monitorDeployment.test.js :: MonitorDeployment > #monitorDeployment() > when monitoring removals > should stop if the deployment is unavailable and the action is "remove"
